title: intent init --lang writes AGENTS.md before it declares the languages, so the contract says none are declared
body:
Found on 2026-09-24 by vc's subagent driving `docs/getting-started.md` for the 3.2.1 doc audit, in a scratch project under an isolated HOME on the pair at `4c687eaad`.

Seen: `intent init --lang rust,shell` in a fresh git repository exits 0, prints `declared: rust` and `declared: shell`, and `intent/.config/config.json` holds both -- yet the `AGENTS.md` the same command writes reads, at its line 15, "None declared. Declare the project's languages with `intent lang init <lang>`." The binary writes `AGENTS.md` first, declares the languages afterwards (`render.rs:8534-8539`), and never regenerates it, so one command leaves the agent contract contradicting its own config, with a remedy that `intent lang init` answers "already declared (no change)" and does not clear. `intent lang init` on its own does not regenerate `AGENTS.md` either; `intent doctor` then reports it as a `root-file-behind` advisory, and `intent agents sync` clears it.

Expected: `intent init --lang` writes an `AGENTS.md` that names the languages it declared.

Disposition: vc, 2026-09-24 -- filed for after the stabilisation line: it is outside the shipping-grade test of hv decision 33 (1), because the advisory names it and `intent agents sync` clears it. `docs/getting-started.md` tells the reader to run `intent agents sync` after declaring a language, as built.
